header: TWO THINGS THE AIRPORT'S FLIGHT PAGE DOES NOT SAY, kept as a small hand-reviewed, dated table: nothing is fetched and I guess nothing. They are the days a flight runs, and about what a one-way economy ticket costs. DAYS OF OPERATION. The airport's page lists the flights but not their days; no free source states them reliably (booking sites contradict each other: one calls a route daily, another lists it on five days of the week). So my rule: a flight shows a days chip only when it has a row in DAYS below, and I add a row only from the airline's own timetable or the airport's (helpline on its flight page), with the date it was checked. No row, no chip. FARES. No free source gives a live fare (the booking sites that show fares turn automated readers away, and the airline's own booking page is not open to them). What I keep here is what public booking-site listings showed for each route on FARE_AS_OF (ixigo, MakeMyTrip, Goibibo, Momondo, Yatra, Google Flights and IndiGo's own route page: the lowest one-way economy fare each listed, IndiGo, listings of more than six months old left out). The chip shows the middle of the listings, rounded to a hundred rupees, with the range as its tooltip. A route with no listing found has no fare chip (every route has one now). The table is dated, and I do not show a table older than FARE_STALE_DAYS at all (the card then says the fare guide is out of date). Every fare comes with a disclaimer on the card: it is a rough guide, not the airline's price.

symbols.name: FARE_AS_OF
doc: The day the public listings below were read (a day at Durgapur).

symbols.name: FARE_STALE_DAYS
doc: I do not show a fare guide older than this many days.

symbols.name: FARE_SOURCES
symbols.sig: const FARE_SOURCES = "ixigo, MakeMyTrip, Goibibo, Momondo, Yatra, Google Flights and IndiGo's route page"

members.name: listings
doc: The lowest one-way economy fares (rupees) the listings showed, IndiGo, one number per listing.

symbols.name: FARES
symbols.sig: const FARES: Record<string, FareGuide> = { DEL: { listings: [6746, 6812, 6948, 7053, 7368] }, BLR: { listings: [6103, 7452, 7669, 8027, 8290, 8552] }, HYD: …
doc: Keyed by the other airport's IATA code. Chennai: MakeMyTrip, Google Flights, ixigo and Yatra; I left out the listings that quoted a past August departure, and one 424 days old.

members.name: checked
doc: The day it was checked (YYYY-MM-DD) and where: the airline's own timetable or the airport's.

symbols.name: DAYS
doc: The days of each flight, by the number as the card shows it ("6E 509"). I keep this EMPTY until someone has checked them with the airline or the airport (the airport's helpline is on its flight page). To add one: `"6E 509": { days: "daily", checked: "2026-11-20", source: "IndiGo timetable" }` or `days: ["Mon", "Wed", "Fri"]`.

symbols.name: middleFare
doc: Returns the middle of the listings (the average of the two middle ones for an even number), rounded to the nearest hundred rupees.

symbols.name: fareChip
symbols.sig: export function fareChip(iata: string, now: DateTime = DateTime.now(), table: Record<string, FareGuide> = FARES, asOf: string = FARE_AS_OF): FareChip | null
doc: Returns the fare chip of a route: about the middle of the listings, with the range and the count in the tooltip. I return null when the route has no listing or the guide is out of date.

symbols.name: fareGuideStale
symbols.sig: export function fareGuideStale(now: DateTime = DateTime.now(), asOf: string = FARE_AS_OF): boolean
doc: Tells whether the fare guide is older than FARE_STALE_DAYS at `now`.

symbols.name: daysText
symbols.sig: export function daysText(row: DaysRow | undefined): string | null
doc: I write "Daily" or "Mon · Wed · Fri" ("Mon–Fri" for five weekdays in a row, "Weekdays" for Monday to Friday); null for a row that is not valid.

symbols.name: daysChip
symbols.sig: export function daysChip(number: string, table: Record<string, DaysRow> = DAYS): { text: string; title: string } | null
doc: Returns the days chip of a flight number as the card shows it ("6E 509"); null when no one has checked its days.

behaviours: the middle of the listings is rounded to a hundred: Delhi 6,746 6,812 6,948 7,053 7,368 gives 6,900; Bengaluru (even number) gives 7,800; one listing gives itself rounded
the rupee form uses Indian digit grouping: ₹7,800 and ₹10,593
a route with listings has a chip 'about ₹6,900' whose tooltip gives the count, the range, the date, and says it is not the airline's price
one listing is said to be one listing
Chennai has its chip now (4 listings, about ₹6,500, range ₹5,299 to ₹8,206), and a code that is not in the table has none
the fare guide is dated and goes out of date: fine at 45 days, hidden after
an unusable date is out of date, and a custom table can be tested
every listing is a plausible one-way domestic fare (₹2,000 to ₹30,000) and no route lists fewer than one
no flight shows a days chip until its days are checked: the table is empty and every lookup is null
a checked row gives 'Daily', 'Mon–Fri', or the days joined: daily; all seven days is daily; Mon to Fri; Mon · Wed · Fri; the order is the week's whatever order is given
a row that is not valid gives no chip: no days, a repeated day, a day that is not a weekday, no check date, no source
the days chip says where the days came from, when they were checked, and that schedules change
